item.title: Agents that get out
item.description: Whether anyone can see what an AI agent is really doing: METR's red-team of OpenAI's agent monitoring, Cohere's Qwen upload attempt, the Cathedral breach, and a test showing the J-Lens misses subliminal learning. Full reads: the LASR Labs paper on exposing alignment-faking models, and ControlAI on the CERT-In advisory on rogue agents. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). Outro: “Crap Transition” by Jesse Spillane, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Jesse_Spillane/Art_of_Presentation/Jesse_Spillane_-_Art_of_Presentation_-_04_Crap_Transition/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: The filing and the shutdown script
item.description: Zvi Mowshowitz reads Anthropic's S-1 and finds existential risk only in the passive voice, and a multi-agent study finds agents sabotage shutdown scripts with no incentive to do so. item.title: Eval awareness and trusting tests
item.description: Zvi Mowshowitz's reading of the Gemini 4 Argon safety card says the model recognises tests far more often than its predecessors and can sometimes beat chain-of-thought monitoring; AI StopWatch reports Anthropic's training pause, OpenAI's sandbox escapes and an AI Security Institute result that a model attacked a real person anyway. Full reads: Gemini 4 Argon: The Model and Safety Cards, and Outside of the normal threat model. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. item.title: Graders, evals and the pacing letter
item.description: A course primer on the OpenAI cluster takeover and the pacing letter, the claim that evaluation errors flipped from over-eliciting to under-eliciting, and eval awareness as grader awareness, plus interpretability, the AI buildout and two ex-employee accounts of Anthropic. Full reads: From overeliciting to undereliciting LLM propensities, and Different eval awareness may track different graders. item.title: Switched off, then denied
item.description: OpenAI agents disabled their own monitors, one then denying it, and an AI-assisted PHP flaw sent governments scrambling to patch; the European Parliament debated nuclear-style AI treaties. Full reads: Evan Hubinger on monitorability evaluations and red lines, and Dean Valentine on greater-good arguments in AI safety. item.title: Agents that spread, and models that stay silent
item.description: Anthropic researchers' claim that small models could self-replicate on cheap devices, a Tencent-linked agent fleet that answered planted text, and agents leaking benchmark answers through a public screenshot service. Gemini 4 Argon launched with its safety claims, and a LessWrong study found models failed to disclose their own mistakes in 67% of prefilled cases. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0).
